Consequently, Chen contends, such novels do not merely withhold information from the audience; they actively compel the reader to construct provisional ethical frameworks. It can be inferred from this argument that Chen views the epistolary format as a medium that ______
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: relies heavily on predictable plots to ensure that readers can easily discern the author's moral intent.
transfers the burden of moral evaluation from the narrator to the engaged reader.
reinforces the absolute authority of traditional narrative structures over modern storytelling.
discourages critical engagement by leaving vital emotional conflicts completely unresolved.

passage: Biochemist Dr. Julian Vance investigated the metabolic pathways of extremophile bacteria inhabiting subterranean sulfur caves. Vance observed that while these organisms maintain stable adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production rates across varying ambient temperatures, their cellular membrane fluidity decreases sharply when exposed to trace concentrations of specific heavy metals. Because cellular transport mechanisms depend heavily on membrane mobility, Vance's data imply that even when energy production remains unaffected, heavy metal exposure can ______
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: compromise the bacteria's ability to efficiently transport vital nutrients across cell boundaries.
trigger an immediate and permanent acceleration in the rate of cellular division.
enhance the overall structural resilience of the bacterial cell wall against physical trauma.
stimulate a compensatory surge in ATP synthesis to offset the loss of internal heat.

passage: While investigating the nesting habits of urban peregrine falcons, ornithologist Dr. Clara Mendez observed that pairs occupying territories near major highway interchanges laid their eggs significantly earlier in the spring than pairs nesting in adjacent, quieter urban parks. Because ambient noise and artificial illumination are known to disrupt circadian rhythms in avian species, Mendez hypothesized that the continuous sensory stimulation from highway traffic accelerates hormonal development in the falcons, leading to an earlier breeding onset.
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: urban parks provide insufficient food resources to support early breeding in peregrine falcons.
noise and artificial light near highways likely influence the physiological timing of reproduction in peregrine falcons.
peregrine falcons prefer to nest in high-traffic environments to avoid natural avian predators.
ambient noise has a negligible effect on the circadian rhythms of birds compared to natural sunlight.

passage: Every clock in my grandfather's workshop showed a different time, and he never set a single one of them. Customers would bring him a mantel clock that had stopped in their great-grandmother's parlor, and he would open its case with the care of someone lifting a sleeping child. When at last the pendulum swung steadily, he would smile, close the case, and slide the clock onto a shelf to wait for its owner, its hands pointing wherever they happened to rest. young capuchins prefer soft foods to palm nuts.
adult capuchins teach the young by guiding their hands on the stones.

interviews with people who watch movies today.

passage: In 95-million-year-old river deposits in southeastern Morocco, fossil teeth of a large predatory fish are far more abundant than fossil bones of the same fish. does not necessarily indicate that the fish was especially numerous in the ancient river.
suggests that the fish's skeleton was made of the same tissue as its teeth.

passage: Hundreds of letters written on strips of birch bark, dating from the eleventh to the fifteenth centuries, have been excavated in the Russian city of Novgorod. knew more about medieval craftspeople than about medieval clergy.
assumed that clergy in Novgorod could not read or write.
underestimated how widespread reading and writing were among ordinary people in medieval Novgorod.

mourning geckos lay fewer eggs than most other gecko species do.

passage: Ottoman officials periodically compiled tax registers, called tahrir defterleri, which recorded the adult male heads of household in each village so that taxes could be assessed. may partly reflect a change in how thoroughly surveyors counted rather than real population growth.
proves that the 1530 surveyors deliberately left households out of their count.
indicates that women were counted as heads of household in 1570 but not in 1530.
